title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 22
paragraphs: Thrasybulus did this and made this proclamation so that the herald from Sardis would see a vast quantity of provisions carelessly piled up and the people feasting, and would report it to Alyattes. And in fact that is what happened. The herald saw it, delivered the king of Lydia's message to Thrasybulus, and returned to Sardis; and, as I am informed, the peace that was made came about simply because of this. Alyattes, who had imagined there was a severe famine in Miletus and that the people had been ground down to the extreme of misery, heard from the herald when he returned from Miletus the exact opposite of what he had supposed. Afterwards peace was made between them on terms of mutual guest-friendship and alliance, and Alyattes built two temples to Athena at Assesos in place of the one, and himself recovered from his sickness. So much, then, for the war waged by Alyattes against the Milesians and Thrasybulus.
